notes: **Presenter:** Mark. One person, one list, in video order.
**Order of the day:** do the Qube run first (A4–A11, one continuous screen recording), pick version A or B from it, then film the talking head (A0) with that version.
**Before recording anything:** the Qube team connects Claude to Qube on Mark's laptop. Don't show any install commands, API keys, emails or file paths.

open.text: Pick version A or B from A8 vs A9 (rule in A9). Send INK the A8, A9 and A11 screenshots and the picked version, and the Script Room copy gets the matching lines 6 and 8.

The third claim ("ChatGPT just killed the financial advisor") is the Director's fill, yours to swap. A fourth, if you want it: "Codex just killed Wall Street." (adds 5 words, about 2s, takes A to 152 words, about 51s; still under 60s).
M14 opens on the Grok claim too. Give the two different first frames (M15's is card A1 already stamped).
If Qube won't load SPY, tell INK which US stock you used instead; spoken lines 3 and 6 change to match.

rows.how: Phone vertical (9:16), eye level, office lights on, lock focus. 1. Three separate takes, one per claim, said loud and fast like a hype ad: "Grok just killed day trading." / "Claude just killed finance." / "ChatGPT just killed the financial advisor." 2. Then lines 1–11 in one take, flat and straight on line 1, with the version (A or B) you picked for lines 6 and 8. 3. Then line 5 again with a hand half over your eyes, and line 7 again as a tight close-up.

Canva, 1080×1920, dark #0B0F14 background. Headline in Inter Bold 96px, white, centred: "GROK JUST KILLED DAY TRADING". A red #EF4444 rubber-stamp graphic reading "KILLED", rotated 12°, over the right half. Our own design: no real news outlet's logo, font or layout, no numbers. Export PNG, plus a second PNG with the stamp cracked (for 37s).
Same style as A1: "CLAUDE JUST KILLED FINANCE". Two PNGs (stamp, stamp cracked).
Same style as A1: "CHATGPT JUST KILLED THE FINANCIAL ADVISOR" (two lines). Two PNGs.

Start one continuous screen recording here and don't stop it until A11. 1. Terminal app, dark theme, font 22, full screen. 2. Type `claude`, press Enter. 3. Hold 2s on the screen showing Qube is connected. Hide anything with an email, key or file path.

rows.file: same recording · about 15s, sped up in the edit
rows.how: In the same Claude session, type exactly, don't paste: `Build the best strategy you can for the S&P 500. Use SPY in Qube, start with $10,000, test it on the last five years of prices, and show me every trade.` Press Enter.

rows.file: same recording · up to 60s, sped up
rows.how: Keep recording while Claude builds it in Qube. When Qube shows the strategy's four sections (when to buy, when to sell, how much, when to get out), hold 3s on that screen.
rows.what: Claude builds the strategy in Qube

rows.file: same recording · up to 60s, sped up
rows.how: Mark clicks Run in Qube himself (line 5: "I hit run"). Keep recording the whole run. Don't change anything Claude built.

Open Qube's result summary. Hold 4s so the final value, total return, period and number of trades are all readable. Screenshot it too. **CHECK: write down the start date, end date and starting amount shown. Don't change any number, and don't rerun to get a better one.**

In the same Claude session, type exactly: `Now test just buying SPY on the first day and holding it to the last day. Same dates, same $10,000.` Press Enter, run it in Qube, open the result summary, hold 4s. Screenshot it. **CHECK: same start date, end date and starting amount as A8. If they don't match, stop and send Mark both screenshots. Note whether Qube's hold result includes dividends (write down Qube's exact wording), so the editor labels it "price only, no dividends" or uses Qube's wording.** **PICK THE VERSION: A8's final value above A9's = version A, unless it wins only by a hair (about 7% or less, roughly five years of dividends): then send Mark both screenshots before picking A. A8's final value below A9's = version B. Equal, or anything else: stop and send Mark both screenshots.**

Back on Claude's strategy (A8), open the full trade list. Scroll it top to bottom slowly, about 6s, so losing trades are readable. Screenshot three losing trades you can point to (for version A's "here, here, and here"). **CHECK: fewer than three losing trades: tell INK the count, and line 8A says "here" that many times. None: send Mark the screenshot before filming.**

Open Qube's view that shows the worst drop (the equity chart and the biggest drop figure). Hold 4s. Screenshot it. Stop the recording. **CHECK: the worst-drop figure on screen is the one the editor points to at the end of line 8 (about 35–36s). Don't retype it on a card.**
Chrome, full screen, zoom 125%, no tabs or bookmarks: open https://www.tqx.ai/igqube2, scroll slowly to "Start free" and "Free · no card required".
Full screen #0B0F14, "Comment QUBE" centred, Instrument Serif 88px white, "QUBE" in gold #E8B04B. 2s.

notes: **Original video:** none — Mark's own concept (Oct 28). No other creator's Reel, face, handle, post or footage anywhere in the video.

**Rhythm:** the hook is a parody of the "AI just killed X" genre, so play it loud and fast: one headline card every 1.6s, a slam and a whoosh on each, Mark sells each claim dead serious, like a hype ad, no wink (a wink kills the stop). Then on "Everybody says this." everything stops dead: music cut, no cards, Mark flat and straight to camera. From line 2 it's Mark's real screen, a cut or zoom every 1.5–2s.

**Layout:** talking head with the screen recording in the top third (1080×640), Mark below. Full screen for the claim cards and for the trade list in lines 7–8. Captions 1–3 words, Inter Bold 58px, key words in gold.
**Version:** build the version Mark picked after his run (A or B, lines 6 and 8). Times are estimates at Mark's 3.0 words a second; re-time to the real take.
